quizData.question: What are the three fundamental components of an object in Object-Oriented Programming?
choices: Attributes, State, and Behavior
Classes, Methods, and Packages
Encapsulation, Inheritance, and Polymorphism
Variables, Constants, and Data Types

quizData.question: What is the primary purpose of using the `this` keyword as `this.variableName` inside a constructor or setter method?
quizData.answer: To eliminate shadowing and distinguish instance variables from constructor parameters of the same name.
choices: To eliminate shadowing and distinguish instance variables from constructor parameters of the same name.
To call a static method from the parent class.
To make the instance variable immutable and final.
To allocate new memory on the heap.

quizData.question: What is Constructor Chaining and how is it accomplished in Java?
quizData.answer: When a constructor invokes another constructor in the same class using `this(...)` as the first statement.
choices: When a constructor invokes another constructor in the same class using `this(...)` as the first statement.
When a subclass overrides the constructor of its superclass.
When multiple constructors are declared with the private access modifier.
When constructors are executed repeatedly inside a while loop.
Compilation error

quizData.question: Where must `this(...)` or `super(...)` constructor calls be placed in a constructor body?
quizData.answer: Strictly as the very first statement of the constructor body.
choices: Strictly as the very first statement of the constructor body.
Anywhere before returning from the constructor.
At the very end of the constructor body.
Inside a finally block.

quizData.question: What happens if a parent class defines ONLY a parameterized constructor `public Person(String name)` and the child class defines no constructors?
quizData.answer: A compilation error occurs because the compiler tries to insert an invisible `super()` call to a non-existent no-arg parent constructor.
choices: A compilation error occurs because the compiler tries to insert an invisible `super()` call to a non-existent no-arg parent constructor.
The program compiles and runs with name set to null.
The JVM automatically generates a parameterized constructor for the child.
The child class inherits the parameterized constructor directly.
Compilation error

quizData.answer: A static method cannot directly call a non-static instance method or variable without an object reference.
choices: A static method cannot directly call a non-static instance method or variable without an object reference.
`num` must be declared inside the `main` method.
`display()` must have a return type of int.
`main` cannot be declared public.

quizData.question: What is a necessary design step to make a class completely immutable in Java?
quizData.answer: Declare all fields private and final, provide no setter methods, and initialize all fields via constructor.
choices: Declare all fields private and final, provide no setter methods, and initialize all fields via constructor.
Declare the class as abstract and provide synchronized setter methods.
Make all fields public static.
Extend the class from `java.lang.Immutable`.

quizData.question: In the `BloodData` case study, if the default constructor sets `bloodType = "O"` and `rhFactor = "+"`, what will `new BloodData().display()` print?
choices: O+
A+
null+
Compilation error

quizData.question: Are constructors inherited by subclasses in Java?
quizData.answer: No, constructors are not members of a class and are never inherited, though they can be called via `super()`.
choices: No, constructors are not members of a class and are never inherited, though they can be called via `super()`.
Yes, all constructors are inherited with the same access modifier.
Yes, but only default no-arg constructors are inherited.
Yes, if marked with the `inherits` keyword.
A B
B A
B
A
